quickFacts.label: Language
quickFacts.detail: English widely spoken by younger generation

periods.title: Old Town & Gediminas Tower
periods.text: Start at Cathedral Square (Katedros aikštė) — the symbolic heart of Lithuania. Climb Gediminas Tower (€6) on the castle hill for a panoramic view of the terracotta-roofed old town, the largest baroque old town in Eastern Europe and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Descend through the park and walk Pilies gatvė — the main old town street lined with cafés, amber shops, and street musicians.
periods.tip: Find the "Stebuklas" (miracle) tile in Cathedral Square — stand on it, spin, and make a wish. Locals do it unironically.

periods.title: Užupis Republic & Churches
periods.text: Cross the bridge into Užupis — Vilnius's self-declared independent republic of artists, bohemians, and dreamers. Read the Užupis Constitution (displayed in 30+ languages on a wall on Paupio gatvė) — "Everyone has the right to be happy." Visit the Gate of Dawn (Aušros Vartai) with its miraculous icon, and Sts. Peter and Paul's Church — 2,000+ white stucco figures covering every surface. Lunch at Bistro 18 for Lithuanian dishes (mains €7–12).
periods.tip: Užupis celebrates its independence day on April 1 — the bridge has passport control and everyone gets a stamp.

periods.title: Vilniaus Gatvė & Nightlife
periods.text: Dinner at Šnekutis — a tiny, legendary beer hall on Polocko gatvė with the cheapest draught beer in the old town (€2 for a half-litre) and hearty Lithuanian food. Cepelinai (potato dumplings stuffed with meat) are the national dish — heavy, filling, and utterly satisfying for €4–6. Then explore Vilniaus gatvė for bars — Bix for cocktails, Alaus Biblioteka for craft beer, or Opium for late-night dancing.
periods.tip: Šnekutis has multiple locations — the one on Polocko gatvė is the original and most atmospheric. Cash helpful.

periods.title: Cathedral Square & Gediminas Tower
periods.text: Start at Cathedral Square — Lithuania's symbolic heart where the nation gathers for celebrations and protests. The neoclassical Cathedral is free to enter. Climb Gediminas Tower (€6) on the castle hill for a panoramic view of the largest baroque old town in Eastern Europe. Find the "Stebuklas" (miracle) tile in the square — stand on it, spin clockwise three times, and make a wish. Walk down Pilies gatvė to the old town.
periods.tip: The Stebuklas tile is a genuine Lithuanian tradition — even locals spin on it when passing. Look for the inlaid stone near the belfry.

periods.title: Baroque Churches & Gate of Dawn
periods.text: Vilnius has more baroque churches per square kilometre than almost any city in Europe. Visit Sts. Peter and Paul's Church (free) — the interior has 2,000+ white stucco figures covering every surface, a masterpiece of baroque decoration. Walk to the Gate of Dawn (Aušros Vartai) — the only surviving city gate with a miraculous icon of the Virgin Mary that draws pilgrims. Lunch at Etno Dvaras for Lithuanian cuisine (mains €7–12).
periods.tip: Sts. Peter and Paul's Church is overwhelming — bring binoculars or zoom your camera to see the extraordinary ceiling details.

periods.title: Vilniaus gatvė Dining & Drinks
periods.text: Dinner at Lokys (The Bear) — Vilnius's oldest restaurant in a 15th-century cellar, famous for wild game: wild boar, elk, and beaver tail (yes, beaver). Mains €12–20. It's touristic but genuinely historic. Then explore Vilniaus gatvė — the main bar street. Alaus Biblioteka (Beer Library) has 20+ Lithuanian craft beers on tap (€3–5). Bix does inventive cocktails (€7–9).
periods.tip: Lokys's beaver tail is a genuine Lithuanian delicacy — it's classified as fish by the Catholic church and tastes like rich dark meat.

periods.title: Užupis — The Artists' Republic
periods.text: Cross the bridge into Užupis — Vilnius's self-declared independent republic since 1997. It has its own president, constitution, flag, and anthem. Read the Užupis Constitution on Paupio gatvė (displayed in 30+ languages) — "A cat is not obliged to love its owner, but must help in difficult times." Explore the street art, galleries, and studios. The angel statue in the main square is the neighbourhood's guardian.
periods.tip: Užupis was once the city's poorest, most crime-ridden area — now it's the creative heart. The transformation is inspiring.

periods.title: MO Museum & University Quarter
periods.text: Visit MO Museum (€9) — Lithuania's museum of modern and contemporary art, designed by Daniel Libeskind. The collection covers Lithuanian art from the 1960s onwards, with powerful pieces from the Soviet era and independence movement. Then walk through Vilnius University's courtyards (€1.50) — one of Europe's oldest universities (1579) with beautiful frescoed halls and 13 interconnected courtyards.
periods.tip: MO Museum is free on the first Wednesday of each month — the Soviet-era art collection is particularly compelling.

periods.title: Šnekutis & Nightlife
periods.text: Start at Šnekutis on Polocko gatvė for Vilnius's cheapest draught beer (€2/half-litre) and Lithuanian food. Try cepelinai — enormous potato dumplings stuffed with meat, the national dish (€4–6). Then bar-hop: Špunka for natural wines in a cozy cellar, Keulė Rūkė for cocktails in a converted bathhouse, or Pablasé for late-night techno. Vilnius nightlife is cheap and genuinely good.
periods.tip: Šnekutis is cash-friendly — bring small bills. The beer is local, unpasteurised, and changes regularly.

periods.title: Bus to Trakai Island Castle
periods.text: Bus from Vilnius bus station to Trakai (30 min, €2). Walk 2km through the town to Trakai Island Castle — a stunning 14th-century red-brick fortress on an island in Lake Galvė, once the seat of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. The castle museum (€10) covers Lithuanian medieval history. The setting — red towers rising from blue lake water, surrounded by forested shores — is one of the most photogenic in the Baltics.
periods.tip: Take the first bus (around 8:30am) to have the castle to yourself — tour groups arrive from 11am.

periods.title: Lake Galvė & Karaim Culture
periods.text: Rent a kayak or paddleboard on Lake Galvė (€8–12/hour) for views of the castle from the water. Then explore Trakai's unique Karaim heritage — a small Turkic community brought here by Grand Duke Vytautas in the 14th century. Visit the Kenesa (Karaim prayer house) and eat kibinai — traditional Karaim pasties filled with mutton and onion (€3–4 each). They're Trakai's signature food.
periods.tip: Kibinai from Senoji Kibininė or Kybynlar are the originals — avoid the tourist stalls near the castle car park.

periods.title: Return & Farewell Dinner
periods.text: Evening bus back to Vilnius. Farewell dinner at Sweet Root — one of Lithuania's best restaurants, focusing on foraged and fermented ingredients from the Lithuanian countryside (tasting menu ~€55). Or keep it budget at Forto Dvaras for traditional Lithuanian food at honest prices (mains €6–10). End the night in Užupis — a quiet drink on the riverbank, watching the old town glow.
periods.tip: Sweet Root's fermentation-focused tasting menu is a revelation — book at least a week ahead. It's worth the splurge.

periods.title: Cathedral Square & Gediminas Tower
periods.text: Start at Cathedral Square — Lithuania's heart. The neoclassical Cathedral is free. Climb Gediminas Tower (€6) for a panorama of the largest baroque old town in Eastern Europe — a UNESCO site. Find the Stebuklas tile, spin three times, and make a wish. Walk down Pilies gatvė — the main artery lined with cafés, amber shops, and buskers. The baroque architecture here rivals Prague.
periods.tip: The Stebuklas tile is near the belfry — stand on it, spin clockwise three times, and make a wish. Locals still do it.

periods.title: Churches & Gate of Dawn
periods.text: Visit Sts. Peter and Paul's Church (free) — 2,000+ white stucco figures covering every surface. Walk to the Gate of Dawn — the only surviving city gate housing a miraculous icon that draws pilgrims from across Eastern Europe. See St. Anne's Church — a Gothic masterpiece Napoleon allegedly wanted to carry back to Paris. Lunch at Etno Dvaras for traditional Lithuanian dishes (mains €7–12).
periods.tip: Sts. Peter and Paul's takes time to appreciate — bring binoculars to see the extraordinary ceiling stucco work.

periods.title: Vilniaus gatvė & Dinner
periods.text: Dinner at Lokys — Vilnius's oldest restaurant in a 15th-century cellar. Wild game is the speciality: boar, elk, and the famous beaver tail (mains €12–20). Then Vilniaus gatvė for drinks — Alaus Biblioteka has 20+ Lithuanian craft beers (€3–5), Bix does creative cocktails (€7–9), and Prohibicija is a speakeasy-style bar with a hidden entrance.
periods.tip: Lokys's beaver tail might sound odd but it's a genuine medieval Lithuanian delicacy — rich, dark, and surprisingly good.

periods.title: Užupis Republic
periods.text: Cross into Užupis — self-declared independent since 1997, with its own president, constitution, and anthem. Read the constitution on Paupio gatvė in 30+ languages. Explore street art, galleries, and studios. The angel statue guards the main square. Once the city's roughest neighbourhood, Užupis is now its creative heart — a place where art and community transformed an entire district.
periods.tip: Užupis Independence Day (April 1) features passport control on the bridge — if you're here, get your stamp.

periods.title: MO Museum & University
periods.text: Visit MO Museum (€9, free first Wednesday) — Daniel Libeskind-designed, covering Lithuanian art from the 1960s onwards. Soviet-era pieces are powerful. Then Vilnius University's 13 courtyards (€1.50) — founded 1579, with frescoed halls and a stunning library. Walk through Bernardinų Garden — a recently restored park along the Vilnia River, perfect for a break.
periods.tip: MO Museum's Soviet-era art collection tells Lithuania's story through dissident and underground artists — don't rush it.

periods.title: Craft Beer & Late Night
periods.text: Lithuanian craft beer is excellent and cheap. Start at Šnekutis for €2 half-litres of local draught. Move to Bambalynė for a wider craft selection in a cozy cellar (€3–5). Then Keulė Rūkė — a converted Soviet bathhouse turned cocktail bar (€7–9) with an interior that's genuinely unique. For dancing, Pablasé or Loftas (a massive creative space) host events and DJ nights.
periods.tip: Bambalynė means "bumblebee" — the honey beer (medus alus) is a traditional Lithuanian speciality worth trying.

periods.title: Trakai Island Castle
periods.text: Bus to Trakai (30 min, €2). Walk to Trakai Island Castle — a 14th-century red-brick fortress on Lake Galvė, seat of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. The castle museum (€10) covers medieval Lithuanian history. The setting of red towers on blue water surrounded by forest is extraordinary. This was once the capital of a state stretching from the Baltic to the Black Sea.
periods.tip: Take the first bus to arrive before tour groups — the castle reflected in calm morning water is the best photo.

periods.title: Kayaking & Karaim Culture
periods.text: Rent a kayak on Lake Galvė (€8–12/hour) for castle views from the water. Explore Trakai's Karaim heritage — a Turkic community brought here in the 14th century. Visit the Kenesa prayer house and eat kibinai — traditional pasties with mutton filling (€3–4 each) at Senoji Kibininė. The Karaim are one of Europe's smallest ethnic groups and Trakai is their spiritual home.
periods.tip: Kibinai are Trakai's must-eat — the traditional mutton version is authentic, but the chicken and mushroom versions are also excellent.

periods.title: Return & Riverside Evening
periods.text: Bus back to Vilnius. Evening along the Neris River — walk from the Green Bridge to the White Bridge as the old town lights up. Dinner at Pilies Katpėdėlė (Meat Dumpling) for handmade dumplings (€5–8 per plate) or Queensberry for a more upscale experience (mains €12–18). End with a quiet drink in Užupis by the river — Tores café-bar has a terrace over the water.
periods.tip: The riverside walk between the Green and White bridges at dusk is one of Vilnius's most underrated experiences.

periods.title: Museum of Occupations & Freedom Fights
periods.text: Visit the Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights (€6) — housed in the former KGB headquarters on Aukų gatvė. The basement cells where political prisoners were held and interrogated are preserved, including the execution room. The upper floors document the Soviet and Nazi occupations, the forest brothers partisan resistance, and Lithuania's path to independence. It's powerful, confronting, and essential.
periods.tip: The KGB cells in the basement are the most affecting part — the graffiti scratched into walls by prisoners remains visible.

periods.title: Žvėrynas & Vingis Park
periods.text: Walk across the river to Žvėrynas — a quiet, leafy neighbourhood of wooden houses and wide streets that feels like a village within the city. Browse the independent cafés and bakeries. Then walk through Vingis Park — Vilnius's largest park where 300,000 people gathered during the Singing Revolution in 1988. The forest paths, river, and open meadows are perfect for unwinding after the morning's heavy history.
periods.tip: Žvėrynas means "zoo" in Lithuanian — the neighbourhood was originally a hunting ground for the Grand Dukes.

periods.title: Halės Market & Dinner
periods.text: Explore Halės Market (Halės Turgus) — Vilnius's main market, recently renovated with both traditional stalls and trendy food vendors. Try Lithuanian curd cheese (varškės sūrelis) from a dairy stall. Dinner at Gaspar's for modern Lithuanian cuisine using seasonal, local ingredients (tasting menu €40 or mains €14–18). Then Prohibicija speakeasy for cocktails — find the unmarked door.
periods.tip: Varškės sūrelis (chocolate-coated curd bars) are Lithuania's favourite snack — addictive and available at every supermarket.

periods.title: Bus to Šiauliai & Hill of Crosses
periods.text: Early bus from Vilnius to Šiauliai (2.5 hours, €12). Then local bus or taxi (12km) to Kryžių Kalnas — the Hill of Crosses. Over 200,000 crosses, crucifixes, rosaries, and carvings cover a small hill. Destroyed by Soviets multiple times, locals rebuilt it each time as an act of defiance. The rustling of thousands of crosses in the wind is an unforgettable sound. Pope John Paul II planted a cross here in 1993.
periods.tip: Bring a small cross to leave — adding to the hill is part of the tradition. Simple wooden crosses are sold at the car park.

periods.title: Šiauliai Town & Return
periods.text: Lunch in Šiauliai — a pleasant if unspectacular Lithuanian town. Try Rūta chocolate shop (Lithuania's famous chocolate brand, founded 1913) for handmade truffles and sweets. Walk the pedestrianised Vilniaus gatvė. The Sundial Square has a golden boy statue marking the city centre. Take the afternoon bus back to Vilnius — use the 2.5-hour ride to process the Hill of Crosses experience.
periods.tip: Rūta chocolates make excellent souvenirs — the handmade truffles and marzipan are exceptional quality at Lithuanian prices.

periods.title: Quiet Evening & Reflection
periods.text: After a full day of travel, keep the evening gentle. Walk through the old town as it empties — Pilies gatvė without crowds is a different experience. Dinner at Forto Dvaras for honest, traditional Lithuanian food at the best prices in the old town (mains €6–10) — cepelinai, šaltibarščiai (cold beet soup), and Lithuanian black bread. A final beer at Šnekutis before bed.
periods.tip: Šaltibarščiai (cold pink beet soup) is Lithuania's summer dish — refreshing, beautiful to look at, and deeply satisfying.

periods.title: Paneriai Memorial & Jewish Heritage
periods.text: Take the train to Paneriai (10 min, €1) — the forest site where 100,000 people, primarily the Jewish community of Vilnius, were murdered during the Holocaust. The memorial (free) and small museum are sober and essential. Vilnius was once "the Jerusalem of the North" — home to one of Europe's greatest Jewish communities. Return to the city and walk through what remains of the Jewish quarter around Žydų gatvė.
periods.tip: Paneriai is a place of quiet contemplation — allow time and emotional space. The forest setting makes the horror more profound.

periods.title: Tolerance Centre & Halės Market
periods.text: Visit the Vilna Gaon State Jewish Museum's Tolerance Centre (€4) for the history of Vilnius's Jewish community — from its golden age as a centre of Talmudic scholarship to its near-total destruction. Then walk to Halės Market for a lighter afternoon — browse the food stalls, pick up Lithuanian smoked meats, cheeses, and fresh bread. Lunch at the market's food hall for quick, cheap eats (€4–8).
periods.tip: The Tolerance Centre tells the story of "Vilna" — the Yiddish name for the city and the name used by its Jewish community for centuries.

periods.title: Antakalnis & Dinner
periods.text: Walk through the Antakalnis neighbourhood — elegant streets, embassies, and the beautiful Sapieha Park. Visit the Antakalnis Cemetery where Lithuanian soldiers, partisans, and civilians who died defending the TV tower in January 1991 are buried. Dinner at Ertlio Namas for a medieval Lithuanian feast experience in a 16th-century cellar (tasting menu €30) — mead, game, and period recipes.
periods.tip: Ertlio Namas serves a multi-course medieval meal — it's theatrical but the food is excellent. Book ahead.

periods.title: Bernardinų Garden & Last Walk
periods.text: Final morning in Bernardinų Garden — a beautifully restored park along the Vilnia River near the old town. Walk through the rose garden, cross the wooden bridges, and enjoy the views of Gediminas Tower above the trees. Last coffee at Crooked Nose & Coffee Stories near the university — one of Vilnius's best speciality coffee spots. Walk Pilies gatvė one final time.
periods.tip: Crooked Nose's pour-over coffee is excellent — the interior is tiny so grab a takeaway and drink in the Bernardinų Garden.

periods.title: Souvenirs & Last Cepelinai
periods.text: Last shopping — Lithuanian linen from stores on Pilies gatvė, amber jewellery from the old town shops, Rūta chocolates, and Lithuanian mead (midus) from Halės Market. Final lunch of cepelinai at Forto Dvaras — because you can't leave Lithuania without one more plate of potato dumplings. Walk through Cathedral Square one last time and spin on the Stebuklas tile for luck.
periods.tip: Lithuanian linen is world-renowned for quality — tablecloths, napkins, and towels from Pilies gatvė shops make lasting souvenirs.

periods.title: Farewell Dinner
periods.text: Farewell dinner at Sweet Root — Lithuania's most celebrated restaurant, focusing on foraged, fermented, and seasonal Lithuanian ingredients (tasting menu ~€55). Or keep it simple at Šnekutis with a final €2 beer and a plate of cepelinai, surrounded by locals and travelers who've all fallen for this quiet, surprising city. Walk home through the old town one last time — baroque spires against a Baltic sky.
periods.tip: Sweet Root books up fast — reserve a week ahead. If you can't get in, their sister bar Ferment does an excellent shorter tasting.

budgetTips.title: Cheapest beer in Europe
budgetTips.text: Šnekutis serves half-litres of local draught beer for €2. Most old town bars charge €3–5 for craft beer and €7–9 for cocktails. Lithuania is one of Europe's cheapest nights out.

budgetTips.title: Cepelinai everywhere
budgetTips.text: A plate of cepelinai (potato dumplings) costs €4–6 and is a massive, filling meal. Forto Dvaras has the best-value traditional food in the old town — full meals for €6–10.

budgetTips.title: Free old town
budgetTips.text: Most churches are free, Cathedral Square, Gediminas Hill (without the tower), Užupis, Bernardinų Garden, and the street art are all free. You can explore for a full day without spending a cent.

budgetTips.title: Bus travel
budgetTips.text: Buses to Trakai cost €2 each way (30 min). City buses cost €1 from the driver or €0.65 with a Vilniečio Kortelė transport card. Walking covers most of the old town.

budgetTips.title: Museum free days
budgetTips.text: MO Museum is free on the first Wednesday. Many museums offer discounts for students. Gediminas Tower is €6 but the hill itself is free with great views.

budgetTips.title: Market eating
budgetTips.text: Halės Market has cheap, fresh food — sandwiches from €2, soups from €3, and the food court upstairs has full meals for €5–8. Better value than any restaurant.

budgetBreakdown.notes: Market food & Forto Dvaras → restaurants → tasting menus
Free sights & 1 museum → multiple museums → guided tours
Šnekutis beer → craft bars → cocktail lounges

practicalInfo.title: Visa & Entry
items: Schengen Zone — EU/UK/US/Canadian citizens stay up to 90 days visa-free
Vilnius Airport (VNO) is 7km from the centre — train runs direct (12 min, €1) or bus 1 (20 min, €1)
Lux Express buses connect Vilnius to Riga (4 hours, €15) and Tallinn (9 hours, €25) — a great Baltic circuit

practicalInfo.title: Health & Safety
items: No special vaccinations required. Tap water is safe to drink throughout Lithuania
Vilnius is very safe — one of Europe's safest capitals. Standard precautions for nightlife areas
European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) covers EU citizens. Pharmacies (vaistinė) are well-stocked

practicalInfo.title: Getting Around
items: City buses and trolleybuses cost €1 from the driver or €0.65 with a Vilniečio Kortelė transport card
The old town is very walkable — Užupis, Cathedral Square, and the Gate of Dawn are all within 15 minutes
Bolt (founded in nearby Estonia) is the cheapest ride-hailing option. Cross-city rides cost €3–6

practicalInfo.title: Connectivity
items: Free WiFi widely available in cafés, restaurants, and public spaces. Lithuania has excellent 4G/5G coverage
EU roaming free for EU plans. Non-EU visitors: Telia or Bitė tourist SIMs from €5 for 5GB at the airport
Download Bolt for rides, Trafi for public transport, and 1188.lt for local business searches

practicalInfo.title: Money
items: Lithuania uses the Euro (€). ATMs are common — Swedbank and SEB machines have fair rates. Avoid Euronet
Cards accepted in most places. Cash useful for markets, Šnekutis, and small food vendors
Tipping: not traditional in Lithuania. Rounding up or leaving €1–2 at restaurants is appreciated, never expected

practicalInfo.title: Packing Tips
items: Layers essential — summers are pleasant (16–24°C) but evenings cool quickly. Rain possible year-round
Comfortable walking shoes for the old town's cobblestones and Gediminas Hill
A warm layer even in summer — Baltic evenings can be surprisingly cool, especially by the river

culturalTips.title: Cepelinai
culturalTips.text: Cepelinai (zeppelin-shaped potato dumplings stuffed with meat or curd) are the national dish. They're enormous, filling, and beloved. Eat them with sour cream and bacon bits. One plate is often enough for two.

culturalTips.title: Beer Traditions
culturalTips.text: Lithuania has a 1,000-year beer culture with farmhouse brewing traditions. Try kaimiškas alus (farmhouse ale) — unfiltered, slightly sour, and completely different from mainstream beer. Šnekutis sources from small farms.

culturalTips.title: Nature & Paganism
culturalTips.text: Lithuania was the last European country to convert from paganism (1387). Ancient nature worship left deep cultural marks — many Lithuanians maintain a spiritual connection to forests, rivers, and the changing seasons.

culturalTips.title: Arts & Creativity
culturalTips.text: Vilnius punches far above its weight in arts and culture. Užupis embodies the creative spirit, MO Museum is world-class, and street art covers entire buildings. Lithuanians are proud cultural innovators.

culturalTips.title: Basketball Religion
culturalTips.text: Basketball is Lithuania's true religion. Ask any Lithuanian about the 1992 Olympic team (funded by the Grateful Dead) and watch their eyes light up. If there's a game on, watch it at a bar for an unforgettable experience.

culturalTips.title: Language & Manners
culturalTips.text: Learn "ačiū" (thank you), "labas" (hello), and "prašom" (please/you're welcome). Lithuanian is one of Europe's oldest living languages. Locals are reserved but warm once you connect — respect the quiet.
